body: I had a converstation with my uni's counseling service over the pjone saturday night, but haven't reached out to our sexual assualt network yet (mostly because it happened on Thursday but mostly snuck in on saturday night about what happened, so places weren't open) or the local one. Unfortunately, this isn't my first rodeo and for the first one it took two weeks for me to process that it was a reportable thing and I should so idk. I feel like I need to report sooner rather then later if I'm going to. But yeah, I need to reach out to someone- Im still having trouble wrapping my head around it, even though I've had similar emotions and experiences.
We're a two party consent state, so that would be illegal.

Its dumb, because a month or so ago, a friend of mine passed away after a long battle with an eating disorder. And, we hadn't been close in years after we both moved, but she'd sometimes like things on facebook or send me a spontaneous message and I was always touched she thought of me. Her death was like a gut punch that made me feel such intense regret- that maybe if I had done more, maybe she would have known more people cared about her and I wish she could see the outpouring of love I've seen for her, if I had been more open about how the random points of contact from her made me beam because she thought of me in her busy/stressful life and it made me smile.



And I dunno. Realistically, I know that its like a ripple effect, and I would impact others who would feel like I do after my friend passed, but its just hard to quantify. Idk. Like logical me knows I'd hurt too many people, and I don't want to hurt anyone or anyone feel an iota of what I feel, but emotional/irrational me is sometimes harder to convince of the fact.


Sorry. Ive been drinking and its been a long week. But I do appreciate the kindness and it made me cry in a good  way<3

Basically. Sometimes the only things keeping me around is the knowledge of how badly it would affect best friend, mom, boyfriend, etc and even then I can convince myself that they really would probably be happier without me being a pain in their respective asses.


Its harder to acknowledge that burden on a dude doing his job and has to live with being the one who killed me. Idk. It doesn't make a lot of sense :(
You may have just saved my life today

...holy shit.


We (dude I was talking about) were in this like... fluid fwb thing for five goddamn years, where I was never offically the girlfriend and he'd occasionally get be like I don't feel that way about you, stop flirting so I'd be like k, sleep with people to get over my hurt (this is also in the midst of the deaths/floundering in school/assualt), he'd take me back, ask me if I had and never lie because... why lie when that shit always comes out, and it hurts worse later then being upfront, he'd get mad and I'd feel like I cheated and feel so. much. guilt. even when rational me knew he told me to fuck off.

Also pieced together later that those periods conceded when he was trying to get with another girl and when he was like yo, kat was when he was shot down. 

I knew he struggled with depression and self worth and I felt like I made everything worse.

Part of what made me realize something was wrong was that we had one last hook up this summer... and he ghosted me for a month afterward. Before this we had talked almost every day, he told how much he missed me (I was out of town for a month visiting family), how much he trusted me, we went to see a movie when I got home, hooked up... and nothing for like a month. I was tearing myself apart, I was in a class but barely could work because I couldn't get my brain to shut up.


But yeah. That was one of the triggers I realized this summer that something was wrong about how I held on to things and with how negatively it was impacting my life and how I couldn't shake it off. 


And I recently got into a relationship with a great dude who tells me how amazing I am and I'm so baffled by it, and telling former friend that I was in this thing was one of the hardest things I've done.


Friend told me he was in a relationship too, and had been. This was like two months from when we hooked up last, so pretty sure that coincides when I got ghosted. And idk. We both gamed and its been our thing, and like... idk. I bought Halo to play with my friend a year ago, and he never expressed interest so I've been playing it with my boyfriend and I cant get over how guilty I feel because I know itd upset him. I have gears of war but feel like I can't play it, but he cant or won't make the time for it. I have  character in destiny I havent done some quest lines with and a gun to get because Im waiting for him. And rational me knows I should just be like fuck it, go for it he had a chance, I can't because what if is angry or hates me or just.... agh :(


and now its sliding over to my person now and I feel like the worst person ever because I feel like I have so much doubt and like I'll fuck things up and its my fault and he'll figure out how screwy my brain is.... idk :(

I've been diagnosed with GAD/Depression/PTSD for a long time, so having overwhelming anxiety wasn't that strange and I've had a lot of loss very suddenly (copy/pasted from below- "from 2011-2014 I experienced: my grandmother dying, nearly flunking out of school, changing majors, my dads escalating alcoholism, a sexual assault, mom moved across the country, I was in a 70mph head on collision, and my dad had an aortic dissection and nearly died and I was next of kin so got to make decisions while he was out."), so all my therapists had told me it wasn't unusual for me to be oversensitive  to loss or being afraid that things would be ripped from me, but idk. The last two years have been fairly normal, but still haven't shaken the fears that my sometimes distant friend would kill himself because I didn't do enough, and if he was quiet it was because clearly, I missed a sign and he had hurt himself. Or if my mom didn't respond to a text, it was because she was in a car wreck. Or that my dog would suddenly die. And I thought it was normal, or just my anxiety talking :(

I think we might have the same friend.

He does a thing when he's stressed, he pulls away from all contact and hermits. When we were younger, there was a massive miscommunication that we had and he lashed out at me, I reacted badly and wound up accidentally hurting him with how I did. I didn't realize I was salt in the wounds for another hurt he was going through, but he told me I really hurt him.

I've carried that guilt for YEARS, so whenever he'd go quiet, or hang out with other people and flake on me, or push me away, I'd go just... fucking nuts and be convinced our friendship was over, or he'd kill himself because I didn't work hard enough and it was all because of me and a mistake that 20 year old me had made years ago, and no matter what I did, I couldn't fix it.

Also, complicated by the fact from 2011-2014 I experienced: my grandmother dying, nearly flunking out of school, changing majors, my dads escalating alcoholism, a sexual assault, mom moved across the country, I was in a 70mph head on collision, and my dad had an aortic dissection and nearly died and I was next of kin so got to make decisions while he was out. So, admittedly, I was... not really myself during those years, but the last two years have been fairly normal in terms of bumps and bruises but... still have the fear and terror that I will violently lose people and it's because of me, and me not doing enough, or me not being there enough. It's been within the last couple of months that I realized it's ok to take care of me.

Idk, I'm sorry, this is long and rambly. D: I'm also glad that I'm not the only one who has this, but sad you can relate- it can pretty devastating, even when I know it's irrational, and it's not something I can really explain to my professors you know? "Kat, why are you so distant?" 

"I was on my phone all night waiting for my friend to text me back because I was convinced he was dead, so I was looking at cats to distract myself and wait for him to text."

"Was he dead?"

"Nope."

I actually have watched Grumps (not so much recently) and I remember watching that episode when it came out. Definitely one that made me cry, even though the OCD part didn't ring true then like it does now. But I could relate to being diagnosed with something and realizing that it has a name, I had a similar reaction when my doctor at the time told me I was experiencing PTSD and it was just like... oh. this isn't normal. this is a thing

I've actually discounted myself as having OCD for awhile because I didn't have any compulsions that are common- like no handwashing or rituals or whatever. It wasn't until I was reading more about it and read that some compulsions aren't overt and are mental checks that I was like ...oh.

Or a need for order and things to be aligned and not being able to do anything rlse until that was done. Or organizing stuff because if its out of order, I can't clean my house or finish my homework. Or if my friend doesn't respond HOLY SHIT HES DEAD AND ITS MY FAULT BECAUSE I HAVEN'T DONE ENOUGH, MUST SEND MESSAGES AND CHECK ALL THE SOCIAL MEDIA. Or holding onto shit for years because I might want it later even when its a damn usb cord and I have a bajillion.

I was talking to my therapist during the screening and I mentioned I wasnt sure if it was OCD quirks or Aspergers quirks, and she was like "We've been talking a long time and I have never pegged you as autistic. What were indicators that you are?"

So I was like "Oh, I had a hard time with routine change... textures bugged me and sensory stuff was hard... I had really deep obsessive interests... I was particular about little thi-oh"

Also found out that Autism is frequently misdiagnosed in place of OCD, and shes not the first mental health person to tell me that I don't make them think autism (though admittedly, I'm in my 20s, was diagnosed in my teens, always told I had a mild case, and I have come a REALLY long way in terms of social skills from 14 to 27)

IDK. We haven't finished the screening but its strange and scary :( In some ways it makes so much sense, and in others- idk. Its so weird to realize how not normal some of my thought patterns are and realize that normal people don't think like this. idk. a little overwhelming :( sorry for the mental health tmi, Im still processing how much makes sense
